title: Cap. 7 Patrum: Augustine De natura & grat. 5 — vessels of mercy only
pass_a_gloss: 3. We will bring forward a third testimony of the same Augustine from the book On nature and grace, chapter 5, which runs thus: Those who are delivered are named not vessels of their own merits, but vessels of mercy. Of whose mercy, if not of him who sent Christ Jesus into this world to save sinners? Whom he foreknew, and predestined, and called, and justified, and glorified. As if he had said that God, by a decree of special mercy, sent Christ for efficaciously and infallibly delivering and saving the predestined; in which sense they alone are called vessels of mercy. It would be superfluous to heap up more from Augustine, whose judgment concerning the absolute predestination of certain persons to eternal life, and concerning the eternal giving of the same to Christ the Mediator that by him they may be led infallibly to that life, is most well known to all who are versed in Augustine. Which predestination, giving, and leading through to eternal life cannot be understood or even thought without this special intention of applying his death and merits to them. See chapter 18 of On the Predestination of the Saints; On the gift of perseverance, chapter 7; On rebuke and grace, chapter 9.
pass_b_english: 3. A third witness from the same Augustine is On nature and grace, chapter 5: Those who are delivered are called not vessels of their own merits, but vessels of mercy. Whose mercy, if not his who sent Christ Jesus into this world to save sinners? Whom he foreknew, predestined, called, justified, and glorified. As if to say: by a decree of special mercy God sent Christ to deliver and save the predestined efficaciously and infallibly — and in that sense they alone are vessels of mercy. Piling up more Augustine would be wasted work. Anyone at home in him knows his teaching on the absolute predestination of some to eternal life, and on the eternal gift of those same persons to Christ the Mediator so that he may lead them to that life without fail. That predestination, gift, and leading cannot be understood — or even thought — without this special intention of applying his death and merits to them. See On the Predestination of the Saints 18; On the gift of perseverance 7; On rebuke and grace 9.
source_text: 3. Tertium ejusdem Augustini testimonium proferemus ex libro De natura & grat. cap. 5. quod ita se habet, Qui liberantur, non vasa meritorum suorum, sed vasa misericordiae nominantur. Cujus misericordiae, nisi illius qui Christum Jesum misit in hunc mundum peccatores salvos facere? Quos praescivit, & praedestinavit, & vocavit, & justificavit, & glorificavit. Quasi dixisset, Deum ex specialis misericordiae decreto misisse Christum pro liberandis & salvandis praedestinatis efficaciter & infallibiliter; quo sensu illi soli dicuntur vasa misericordiae. Supervacaneum esset ex Augustino plura congerere, cujus sententia de absoluta praedestinatione quorundam ad vitam aeternam, deque aeterna datione eorundem Christo Mediatori, ut ab eo infallibiliter perducantur ad eandem, est omnibus in Augustino versatis notissima. Quae praedestinatio, donatio, perductio ad vitam aeternam, absque hac speciali intentione mortem ac merita sua illis applicandi, neque intelligi, neque cogitari potest. Videte caput 18. De Praed. Sanct. De bono persev. cap. 7. De cor. & grat. cap. 9.
